newsitem.title: TURKEY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FENERBAHCE BEAT SCRAPPY GALATASARAY IN ISTANBUL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FENERBAHCE BEAT SCRAPPY GALATASARAY IN ISTANBUL.

text.p: Galatasaray playmaker Gheorghe Hagi was sent off on Sunday as Fenerbahce defeated their Istanbul rivals 3-2.
Fenerbahce, who sacked their Brazilian coach Sebastiao Lazaroni last Thursday, joined Galatasaray at the top of the Turkish league.
Romanian World Cup midfielder Hagi was dismissed in the 78th minute for his second bookable offence when he pushed a Fenerbahce player with the ball at the other end of the pitch.

The result was a triumph for Fenerbahce's new coach Todor Veselinovic who got off to a winning start thanks to a goal from Nigerian striker Augustine "Jay Jay" Okocha and two from Bosnian forward Elvir Bolic.
"We played like men. We are now on equal terms in the championship race," said Ridvan Dilmen, a former Fenerbahce player who will assist Yugoslav Veselinovic.
Bolic's two goals, one from the penalty spot, ended a one-and-a-half month famine and gave Fenerbahce the lead on their home ground after the two sides were level 1-1 at the interval.
The game promised much in the way of entertainment with tickets changing hands at 10 times their face value but in the end the 30,000 crowd witnessed a scrappy, disjointed game played in dense fog.
Okocha gave Fenerbahce the lead in the 15th minute after Bolic's header rebounded off the shoulder of Galatasaray goalkeeper Mehmet Sen but defender Vedat Inceefe equalised just four minutes later.

Fenerbahce controlled the game but were unable to score again until the 52nd minute when Bolic restored their lead with a penalty after Inceefe had tripped Ilker Yagcioglu in the box. A minute later Hagi got his first yellow card for tripping Saffet Sancakli.

Fenerbahce continued to press and were rewarded with a fortunate third goal in the 78th minute. Bolic was again the scorer after Sen made a complete mess of a weak cross and spilled the ball back into his own net.

Substitute Arif Erdem scored a consolation goal from a free kick in the 90th minute but the visiting team never managed to combine well enough to avenge their 4-0 first-half home defeat by Fenerbahce. they were particularly let down by their international striker Hakian Sukur who squandered five clear chances in the first half and was virtually anonymous throughout the second half.
The relief for a Fenerbahce side under new management, was almost tangible.
Lazaroni had been blamed for the club's bad form in the second half of the season, which saw them score just two goals, draw against lowly Izmir team Altay and exit from the Turkish cup.
Fenerbahce chairman Ali Sen said the victory confirmed he was right in changing the coach.
"If you know where to make changes success will follow," he said. "We achieved success with a timely change."
Meanwhile, Galatasaray coach Fatih Terim, who has yet to see his team win this year, said there was no cause for alarm.
"There is no need to panic. We played well at times during the match but we missed some goals we should have had. Despite this result we are still in with the best chance to win the league."

Fenerbahce fans showered the Galatasaray players' bus with plastic bottles and coins as they arrived in the stadium, which was guarded by two thousand policemen. The rival spectators booed and beat drums ceaselessly throughout the match but there was no violence.
Teams:

Fenerbahce - Fevzi Layic, Ilker Yagcioglu, Uche Okechukwu, Jes Hogh, Erol Bulut (Halil Ibrahim Kara), Selahattin Ozbir (Mustafa Dogan, 82), Saffet Akbak, Augustine "Jay Jay" Okocha, Tayfun Korkut, Elvir Bolic, Saffet Sancakli (Tuncay Akgun 70).

Galatasaray - Mehmet Sen, Bulent Korkmaz, Vedat Inceefe, Bekir Gul, Iulian Filipescu, Suat Kaya (Arif Erdem, 62), Tugay Kerimoglu, Georghe Hagi (red card, 78th), Ergun Pembe, Adrian Ilie, Hakan Sukur.
